aifact: CLAUDE.md — The AI Onboarding Document That Replaces Session Re-Explanation
aifactinsight: AI FACT/INSIGHT: CLAUDE.md is a persistent project context file placed at the project root that acts as an onboarding document for Claude Code — the same way you'd brief a new engineer on how a project is structured and what the rules are, CLAUDE.md does that quietly in the background, every session, automatically. Without it, the AI doesn't know your project conventions, constraints, or architecture decisions — forcing you to re-explain things every session. It is fundamentally different from README.md: README.md is for humans (setup steps, links, how to run things); CLAUDE.md is for the AI (architecture, file layout, naming conventions, explicit boundaries). AGENTIC INSIGHT: This represents **'Persistent Agent Context Injection'**. In Claude Code's internal architecture, CLAUDE.md feeds the PROJECT CONTEXT component which flows as CONTEXT into the Core Engine Agent (Think, Plan, Delegate), which then EXECUTES via Capabilities (Bash, Read, Write tools) through the IDE/VS Code/Terminal interface — with Claude Sonnet/Opus providing REASONING via the LLM Intelligence layer. Every line written in CLAUDE.md saves hours later because Claude reads it and follows it across every session, every skill, every agent. SOURCE: LinkedIn Post #CodingTips + Anthropic Claude Code Official Docs
practicalUsage: Place CLAUDE.md at your project root immediately when starting any Claude Code project. Use `/init` to generate a starting draft automatically — it scans your codebase and produces build commands, test instructions, key directories, and detected coding conventions. Follow up with `/memory` to refine it. Never put secrets or credentials in it. Treat it as a living document — update it as your project evolves. CLAUDE.md also supports a hierarchy: `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` for personal preferences across all projects, `./CLAUDE.md` at project root shared via git with your team, and `./src/CLAUDE.md` for subdirectory overrides in monorepos — more specific files take priority.

aifact: CLAUDE.md Five-Section Structure — Project Overview, Architecture, Commands, Conventions, Safety
aifactinsight: AI FACT/INSIGHT: An effective CLAUDE.md should contain five core sections: (1) **Project Overview** — what is this, what tech stack, how is it deployed (2-3 sentences max); (2) **Architecture** — file structure and directory purposes, this is where AI decides 'where things go'; (3) **Commands** — common commands with the right flags so the AI stops guessing; (4) **Conventions** — naming patterns, what to follow, what to NEVER do; (5) **Safety** — what the AI should be careful about and always check before acting. AGENTIC INSIGHT: This represents **'Structured Agent Guardrail Definition'**. The Safety and Conventions sections are the highest-leverage entries — they prevent the AI from taking actions that conflict with project architecture. Concrete example from the source: without CLAUDE.md, asking 'add React component' → AI starts adding React. With CLAUDE.md defining 'no JavaScript, no frameworks,' the same request → AI pushes back: 'This conflicts with project conventions, no JavaScript, no frameworks.' That guardrail behavior is the core value proposition. The mindset shift: Traditional DevOps engineering means write the code; agentic workflows means write the instructions — the quality of your instructions directly determines the quality of your AI output. SOURCE: LinkedIn Post #CodingTips
practicalUsage: Structure your CLAUDE.md in this exact five-section order: Project Overview → Architecture → Commands → Conventions → Safety. Keep Project Overview to 2-3 sentences. The Conventions section should explicitly list both what TO do and what to NEVER do. The Safety section should enumerate what the AI must always check before acting. Never store API keys, tokens, or passwords in CLAUDE.md. Use the `#` key during a Claude Code session to add instructions you find yourself repeating — these accumulate into a CLAUDE.md that genuinely reflects how your team works.

aifact: Vectorless RAG — Hierarchical Tree Indexing Replaces Chunking and Embeddings
